scenes.heading: Handling a customer dispute over completed work

sents.d: Handling a customer dispute over completed work
How you handle the first complaint often decides whether you keep the customer or lose the review.

Listening fully before responding, even when you believe the work was done correctly, de-escalates most disputes faster than immediately defending yourself — many customers mainly want to feel heard before they'll consider a resolution.
Having photos or notes from the job (before/after, materials used) makes disputes far easier to resolve fairly, since you're working from evidence rather than competing memories of what happened.

For a dispute that's genuinely your error, fixing it quickly and without excessive apologizing often turns an upset customer into a loyal one — how you handle a mistake frequently matters more to a customer's long-term opinion than the mistake itself.

take: Listen first, document jobs, and fix genuine mistakes quickly.
